Share VPC/private deployment arm doc and network diagram

summary: Initial security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment modes. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and SSO enforcement, RBAC granularity, audit logs retention and access, encryption (KMS/BYOK/HSM), and data residency/data retention policies. Agreement to exchange certs and schedule a deep-dive around KMS/byok and private network setup.
topics: Encryption at rest / KMS / BYOK / HSM
Hosting modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Asteria CISO), Marcus Cole (VP Eng), Leah Chen (Infra), Omar Haddad (Sec Eng)

00:00 Samantha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is samantha from Redwood Inference, i have diego (SE) with me, quick agenda — security posture discovery, figure out your must-haves for hosted/dedicated/private, and next steps
00:18 Priya: thanks, yeah we wanted to run through our checklist; basically SOC2 evidence, how you do SSO and RBAC, and then encryption/KMS questions. also we have data residency requirements for europe customers and retention rules
00:34 Diego: great, i'll try to capture the technical bits — we support hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private vpc or on-prem. there are nuances in auth/keys depending on mode, so we want to align on your requirements
00:47 Marcus: just to set context, we process financial transactions and pii — our compliance team needs clarity on logs, who can access them and for how long, also key management is important, we prefer BYOK if possible
01:10 Samantha: totally, priya can you share target timeline and any procurement hoops? helps us prioritize whether hosted with specific controls is ok or we should focus on dedicated/private early
01:25 Priya: procurement timeline is pretty standard — RFP in march, security review now, then pilots in april-may. decision timeframe q2. main blocker is SOC2 type II and a clear BYOK path
01:41 Leah: quick Q — for hosted mode, can you do network peering or private links? we try to avoid public internet egress for some traffic
01:55 Diego: yes — hosted can be configured with private networking via cloud provider private link/peering for select customers; Dedicated gives more control (dedicated GPU pools inside our VPC), and Private gives fully customer-managed network, on-prem option. there are tradeoffs with latency and ops overhead
02:20 Omar: on key management, do you offer HSM-backed keys or only cloud KMS? and is there an audit trail for key usage?
02:32 Samantha: we integrate with major KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and support BYOK for dedicated/private. HSM-backed is supported via customer HSM integrations for private deployments. audit logs will show key operations to the extent the KMS reports them — we can surface log events in the console and also stream to customer SIEM
03:00 Priya: what's the model for encryption at rest for cached KV state — i know some runtimes keep prefix cache, how is that handled?
03:12 Diego: good question — we encrypt all disk volumes and data-at-rest. kv cache encryption depends on deployment: hosted uses our managed encryption, dedicated/private can be configured to use customer KMS. there was an instance earlier where docs said KV catch — sorry kv cache — transcription — but yeah it's encrypted
03:35 Marcus: audit logs — can we get immutable, tamper-evident logs and how long do you retain? we might need 7 years for certain records
03:49 Samantha: default retention is 90 days in hosted console, with export capability to customer S3/long-term storage; for Dedicated/Private we can enable extended retention and direct streaming to your storage for archival. immutable/tamper-evident depends on your archive storage (e.g., write-once S3 config) and we provide signed log bundles
04:14 Priya: SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning, we need enforced 2FA. how do you handle SSO for console vs API keys?
04:28 Diego: we support SSO (SAML/OIDC) for the Console and SCIM for automated user provisioning. API access can be restricted by role; we recommend short-lived tokens and integration with your identity provider for session rules. 2FA is enforced via your IdP when configured
04:50 Leah: RBAC granularity — can we define roles at project/model/route level and have audit events show which token/id did what?
05:04 Diego: yes, our RBAC supports org, project, and model-level roles; fine-grained permissions for deploy, read logs, billing view. logs include actor id and token metadata but sometimes token name mapping is noisy in transcripts — but for real logs they include user/email and API key id when available
05:35 Samantha: do you have PCI or financial industry experience?
05:41 Priya: yep that's important; any encrypted payload transit controls or egress policies to third-party plugins?
05:52 Diego: we do a lot of fintech customers; TLS in transit is default, we can disable outbound network egress for private deployments and limit third-party connectors. for hosted customers we offer VPC peering + egress controls and can set allow-lists
06:20 Marcus: procurement will ask for SOC 2 type II, ISO27001, pen test reports, and indemnity language — can you share those certs and the scope of audits?
06:34 Samantha: absolutely — action item to share SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 cert, pen test summary and SOC scope doc. we'll redacted-sensitive IP in reports but provide evidence. we usually send these under an NDA or secure link
06:50 Priya: how about logging access — can we limit Redwood internal support access and have just-in-time access with RBAC & approval?
07:02 Diego: yes for Dedicated/Private we can restrict Redwood support access; support access is logged and requires customer approval for more intrusive ops. Hosted support can get access via a controlled workflow with auditable approvals
07:25 Omar: do you provide a security runbook for incident response and how we can get root cause info quickly?
07:36 Samantha: we have an IR playbook and we can share an exec summary; for customers under enterprise contract we provide deeper details and SLA for incident notifications
07:50 Priya: any model/data residency controls? we need to ensure european customer data stays in eu regions and is not used to fine-tune public models by default
08:05 Diego: yes — data residency is enforced by routing policy and model variants. hosted supports region pinning so requests stay in EU regions; we do not use customer data to train public models unless opted in. model variants for local hosting can also be used in Private deployments
08:28 Marcus: regarding egress logs for generated text, is there a way to redact ppi in logs before storing?
08:40 Diego: we offer configurable scrubbers and redaction at the ingestion layer; for more advanced needs you can run a pre-processing step inside your VPC (private deployment) to strip sensitive fields before sending to inference
09:05 Priya: ok this is good, can you give a concrete example of BYOK flow for dedicated? like key creation, rotation, and how tokens are encrypted with customer keys
09:18 Diego: typical pattern — customer creates a key in their KMS, grant Redwood encryption/decrypt permissions scoped to the key; Redwood uses the key to encrypt model artifacts and cache layers in Dedicated; key rotation supported but requires a rewrap process; we document steps and provide a TF snippet. for private, you keep full control and HSM-backed keys remain in your environment
09:52 Samantha: priya i'm going to note the procurement/contract asks, but diego you'll follow up on the KMS/TF snippet
10:01 Priya: yep, please include any network diagrams for private deployment, also the reqs for on-prem (hardware sizing, GPU types)
10:12 Diego: noted — i'll include an example sizing for t4/v100/a100 depending on throughput, and typical latency metrics we see. there's sometimes confusion in docs between model quantization numbers and kernel selection but we'll be explicit
10:35 Marcus: do you have SOC scope that excludes any specific services? just want to know coverage for key mgmt, logging, and alerting
10:47 Samantha: SOC2 scope covers our production inference control plane and data handling controls; KMS integrations are in scope for Dedicated/Private differently — we'll send the SOC scope doc so you can see exact in-scope systems
11:05 Leah: retention again — default 90 days, but if we need 7 years for some artifacts are you able to export logs to our S3 and ensure immutability?
11:18 Diego: yes, we can ship logs in near-real-time to your bucket and you can set object locks for immutability. for hosted we also provide signed log bundles on request
11:34 Omar: curious about redwood support model — you mentioned just-in-time access, can that be found in contracts?
11:44 Samantha: yes, enterprise terms include support access governance and we can include JIT/approval flow language in SOWs
12:00 Priya: any open vulnerabilities or high-severity CVEs outstanding we should know about?
12:08 Diego: we run continuous scanning; any critical CVEs are patched asap and communicated. we can share our vulnerability disclosure cadence and patch timelines in the security pack
12:25 Marcus: ok costs — dedicated/private have bigger ops costs, how do you help optimize? (batching, quantization, cache)
12:36 Samantha: we surface recommendations in Redwood Optimize — batching and quantization suggestions, and model profiles so you can balance cost vs latency. for dedicated we help size a pool to hit throughput goals while minimizing idle GPU time
12:58 Priya: last one — do you provide SLA for data deletion requests and ability to purge cached prompts/responses?
13:10 Diego: yes, data deletion is supported; for hosted we have deletion workflows and guarantees; for dedicated/private you can run local purge operations. note that backups may need retention windows and we document timelines in the policy
13:28 Samantha: great, sounds like next steps are sharing SOC/ISO certs, KMS/BYOK docs, network diagrams, and schedule the KMS deep-dive. any other open asks?
13:41 Priya: also include pricing guidance for dedicated baseline and private deployment overheads so procurement can start modeling
13:52 Samantha: will do — thanks everyone
14:00 [meeting ends — recording stops]

Notes on transcript quality: some minor ASR errors present (e.g., KV cache -> KV catch, occasional speaker attribution); content checked for key security topics.
